clue.text: Bored, we hear, with landlady's offering

definitions.meaning: bored is said like board, the meals and lodging a guest pays for
what a boarding-house keeper offers overnight guests: a room and a morning meal

explanation.surface: Someone yawns through the lodgings a landlady provides.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works by sound: 'Bored, we hear' gives 'board', as in room and board.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady typically lets out a room for the night with a morning meal included, the classic guesthouse deal.

clue.text: A bit of a short sharp shock?

definitions.text: A bit of a short sharp shock?

parts.words: A bit of a short sharp shock?
parts.note: a shock of hair cut short and stiff is made of many sharp little hairs; one is a bit of it

explanation.surface: A taste of harsh punishment, the kind of brief severity once promised for young offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short sharp shock' was a British slogan for brief harsh punishment; here a 'shock' is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stiff hair, like one on a crew cut or brush, is one tiny sharp part of a shock of hair.

clue.text: Impressions gained by time in studies

indicators.note: the time letter is placed inside the word for studies

parts.note: dens are private rooms for study

explanation.surface: Ideas picked up after time spent in study rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressions here are hollows pressed into a surface, the kind left by a knock on a car door.

clue.text: Unsurpassed APR on line for revisal

indicators.note: something sent for revisal is reworked, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A finance document's interest rate is put on a line to be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal, beyond comparison, is peerless; the French-derived word means exactly that.

clue.text: They put on airs when out

definitions.text: They put on airs when out

parts.words: They put on airs when out
parts.note: not snobs but street performers who play tunes (airs) outdoors

explanation.surface: Snobs who act grand whenever they go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Street musicians perform melodies outdoors for passers-by, so they literally put on airs out of doors.

clue.text: Mark, for example, road in English stately home

indicators.note: the road abbreviation goes inside the word for a stately home

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing house
ST, street, stands for a road

explanation.surface: Giving directions: a road inside an English stately home's grounds, like Mark's.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is strictly a Gospel, not a letter, so the definition is loose: it treats a New Testament book as an example of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of the New Testament include letters to early churches; the setter loosely counts Mark among those scriptural writings.

clue.text: Smooth return-and falls over

indicators.note: a word in return comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Someone smooths things over on the way back and takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to topple or collapse, so 'falls over' fits the verb with its idiom.

clue.text: Argue over change about tea break

parts.note: to alter is to change
C, circa, means about

indicators.note: to break the word tea is to shatter it so its letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: People quarrel about changing the timing of the tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to dispute heatedly, a formal verb for quarrelling.

clue.text: Time to shuffle-nonsense

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with short rocking steps, a kind of shuffle

explanation.surface: Time to shuffle along, as the talk is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffle' looks like an anagram signal but is a walking word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk or writing, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: All out effort

parts.note: in cricket a side's turn at batting ends when all its batsmen are out

explanation.surface: A maximum push, giving everything.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team's turn at the crease is over when ten batsmen are out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team's batting turn lasts until it is all out, so the whole effort is its spell at bat.

clue.text: The state of train that's broken down

indicators.note: a broken-down train's parts are scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Grumbling about how a broken-down train looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a condition of inactivity or resistance to change, a state of rest.

clue.text: Will mates fall out in temporary accommodation?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

indicators.note: mates who fall out break apart, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Will friends quarrel while sharing a campsite shelter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall out' makes STAME; 'Will' looks like the future-tense verb opening a question but is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document leaving a person's property.

clue.text: Keep quiet, showing embarrassment a little bit

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
red is the colour of an embarrassed blush

explanation.surface: Hush, a slight blush is showing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment, as in 'not a shred of evidence'.

clue.text: State train

definitions.meaning: to state is to put into words, to voice
a fast train making few stops

explanation.surface: Naming the national railway service.
explanation.definitionFit: To put feelings into words is to voice them, and a fast service with few stops is a named train type.

clue.text: Novel pocket heater

parts.note: in snooker to pot a ball is to pocket it
a boiler heats water

explanation.surface: A clever little heater to carry in a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a mediocre novel written quickly just to earn money.

clue.text: Half of them support squeeze

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word gives two of its letters, here the back pair

parts.note: a brace is a support or prop

explanation.surface: Half of them back a squeeze, perhaps a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, holding someone tightly in the arms.

clue.text: A star following principal's steps

indicators.note: the star phrase comes after the boss word

parts.note: the principal, the person in charge, is the boss
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity trails behind the head teacher's footsteps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' signals that the star phrase trails the boss; the 's on principal's is just a link, and 'steps' means a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance steps make up the Brazilian bossa nova, so 'steps' stands for the dance by its moves.

clue.text: Honorary head teacher changed ritual

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
a changed word has its letters reordered

explanation.surface: An honorary head teacher altered the school ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular post is one held in name only, like an honorary title without duties.

clue.text: Trade in vehicles

definitions.meaning: to deal or trade, often in illicit goods
cars and lorries moving on the roads

explanation.surface: The business of dealing in cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit dealing is called by the same word as the vehicles crowding the roads at rush hour.

clue.text: Race within a race?

parts.note: a whole meeting of boat contests on water, each heat a contest held inside the larger event

explanation.surface: A contest nested inside another contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A regatta is a meeting made up of several races, so each race is one within the larger event.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing or sailing event made up of a series of boat races is a race meeting, many races in one.

clue.text: Dirty old boy — part of the act!

parts.note: a scene is a part of a play's act

explanation.surface: A dirty old man in the audience is part of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent, a stronger word for smutty or dirty.

clue.text: Supervise circle lines late finish

parts.note: O is a circle by its shape
verse is lines of poetry

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A manager watches the circle line trains finish late.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct, a synonym for supervise.

clue.text: Jumper, half hunter, still came first

indicators.note: the word for still is placed before the half word

parts.note: even, as in 'even better', means still

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word gives three letters, here the back three

explanation.surface: A jumper, half hunter, still won the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is not a sweater: an eventer is a horse in eventing, which includes show jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing horses compete in dressage, cross-country and show jumping, so they are jumpers.

clue.text: Amid stream on Galway river

annotationWithheld.why: Amid stream on Galway river: AMONG is hidden in 'stream on Galway' with 'Amid' the definition, but no word signals the hidden word and 'river' has no job; likely OCR or garbled text, not found in search

clue.text: Heavy blow-nothing gives such enjoyment

parts.note: a gust is a strong blast of wind
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A strong wind with nothing more brings such pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest, so doing something with gusto is doing it with enjoyment.

clue.text: Cook a dinner with eg syrup

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prepare a meal with a sweet syrup, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red pomegranate-flavoured syrup used in drinks.

clue.text: Did nothing after I'd taken the lead

parts.note: led means went in front, took the lead

explanation.surface: Someone loafed once they had gone ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To have idled is to have lazed about, doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Shoots ET in studio

parts.note: to film is to shoot a scene
taken as written

explanation.surface: The alien film ET is shot in a studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A film set is the constructed scene in a studio where filming happens.

clue.text: Divided about books to be highlighted

indicators.note: the divided word goes around the books letters

parts.note: split means divided
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Opinion split about which books deserve attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit up by a spotlight, something is literally highlighted, picked out for attention.

clue.text: Body snatcher? He's looking for company

parts.note: corporate means relating to a body, a corporation
a raider snatches things

explanation.surface: A grave robber searches for someone to keep him company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body snatcher' suggests grave robbing; it is a predator who seizes companies.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporate raider buys up shares to take control of a business, so he is hunting a company.
